summary: Completed fresh native+backend regression run for Vesper parity scope: full native JVM suite, release/debug assemblies, BuildConfig/version validation, and backend external/native-download/trailer contracts.

integration_issues.flow: Native TV visual parity vs authoritative V2 (rows/hero/details/trailer playback on real TV box)
integration_issues.issue: Not provable in this container: no physical Android TV hardware rendering/GPU validation. Robolectric/layout checks and builds passed, but pixel parity and decoder behavior on device remain unverified.

issues: Code review risk: current row geometry math still appears capable of showing more than six posters at normalized width; explicit six-column enforcement is not codified in tests/UI policy yet.
Code review risk: PagedShelfLayout uses scrollToPositionWithOffset(position, 0) ignoring parent paddingTop, which can reintroduce row/header snap mismatch on some viewport combinations.

action_items: Run real-device Android TV parity pass against authoritative V2 recording (1920x1080 mdpi/xhdpi + 1280x720 + 3840x2160) and capture evidence for hero/rows/details/trailer focus behavior.
Add/adjust explicit acceptance test for exactly six visible posters on normalized browse width and verify row snap with parent padding preserved.
Validate NewPipe extraction + decoder playback on hardware (container run used MOCKED/fixture paths for unit-level trailer timing/candidate logic).
critical_code_review_comments: TvViewport context override is correctly scoped to MainActivity and not PlayerActivity; release BuildConfig correctly disables private prefill.
TrailerRepository now has stronger regression coverage for candidate order, fallback, cancellation and URL hardening; however, production parity still depends on on-device extractor/runtime behavior.
Home row/paging behavior still relies on implicit sizing and offset assumptions; enforcing V2-equivalent six-column and snap invariants needs stronger UI-level assertions.

rca of the issue: Main remaining blocker is environment fidelity, not immediate test failure: container/Robolectric confirms contract and logic regressions but cannot prove hardware-rendered pixel parity and decoder behavior on TV box. Additional code-review risks indicate likely geometry mismatch roots (implicit row sizing and zero-offset snapping) behind user-reported visual drift from V2.
